notes.text: Peru's credit system has largely de-dollarised: foreign-currency loans fell from 46.5% of total credit in 2010 to 24.6% in 2023, helped by repo operations and higher reserve requirements on foreign-currency funding after 2013, though the IMF finds the trend has stalled since 2022. A lower dollar share limits households' exposure to sol depreciation, although the IMF judges remaining unhedged dollar credit riskier and recommends targeted macroprudential measures.

sources.title: Peru: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/125)
